sharedGlossary.label: The Model
sharedGlossary.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. Built by the merge, then read by the es-view server and generator. In this flow it is read-only -- the source of truth the selection is validated against and grounded from.

sharedGlossary.label: Local filesystem
sharedGlossary.description: The local filesystem outside the process boundary. Holds the per-flow trace JSONs read as input and receives the merged flows.json written as output (CLI path only; the server keeps the merged model in memory). In this flow it is the source of the REAL code excerpts each grounded projection pulls behind an anchor.

sharedGlossary.label: Viewer
sharedGlossary.description: The human viewing the Event Storming explorer SPA. Here they curate a bundle: right-clicking or clicking 'Add to context' on nodes, whole flows, and hotspots to gather the set they want to hand to Claude, then optionally copying it or leaving it for a connected Claude session to @-mention.

sharedGlossary.label: flows.json
sharedGlossary.description: The persisted canonical model store. A single JSON file assembled and written by the merge, then read back by the es-view server (in-memory) and by the generator. Its 'columns' are the top-level JSON keys: nodes, flows, hotspots, terms, meta (+ version). The authoritative structure is docs/flows-schema.md; the merge code maps the in-memory object onto it.

sharedGlossary.label: Operator
sharedGlossary.description: The developer/orchestrator who runs the recovery CLIs (es-merge, es-generate, demo) and launches es-view. Here they boot the interactive explorer with `npx event-storming-recovery`, `es-view`, or `npm run preview`.

sharedGlossary.label: Selection / Context bundle
sharedGlossary.description: The live 'what am I looking at / what have I gathered' state for one es-view run, held purely in memory and shared same-process between the SPA API and the MCP bridge. This flow uses its bundle facet: an insertion-ordered set of typed refs { type: node|flow|hotspot, id }; the selection tracer uses the selection facet on the same object.

sharedGlossary.label: Connected Claude session
sharedGlossary.description: A Claude session connected to the es-view MCP endpoint (same process as the SPA). It reads the curated bundle by @-mentioning the event-storming://selected-nodes resource, receiving the whole gathered set as grounded markdown so a refactor request is anchored to real files, not just labels.

sharedGlossary.label: Raw model payload
sharedGlossary.description: The whole resolved model plus provenance meta, returned as one JSON payload from GET /api/model (the same projection the MCP list_model tool exposes). The SPA holds it in a single React context and re-derives every tab from it -- it is the substrate, not a rendered view.

sharedGlossary.label: Data-model tab
sharedGlossary.description: The physical storage the code actually touches, as a tree: server ▸ database ▸ table ▸ column, and for each table the behavioral nodes that write/read/project it. Answers 'what tables does this touch / where does this data live / who writes this table'. Returned by list_data_model and shown in the Data-model tab.

sharedGlossary.label: MergeTraces
sharedGlossary.description: Fold every per-flow trace document into one canonical, validated model. Nodes are unioned by global id, flows/hotspots/terms accumulated, derived meta computed, and all invariants checked before the model is returned.

sharedGlossary.label: GenerateViews
sharedGlossary.description: Render the canonical flows.json into the two shipped views: a Graphviz flows.dot digraph (one cluster per flow, event-storming palette) and a self-contained interactive explorer.html with the whole model inlined. Invoked as the second synchronous step of the demo wrapper.

sharedGlossary.label: Graphviz flows.dot
sharedGlossary.description: The Graphviz digraph (flows.dot): one cluster per flow with event-storming-colored stickies and labeled edges, rendered offline (e.g. `dot -Tsvg`) or in a Graphviz viewer to read the whole board at a glance. Physical storage nodes and any edge touching them are deliberately excluded.

sharedGlossary.label: Interactive explorer.html
sharedGlossary.description: The self-contained interactive Event Storming explorer: a single HTML file with the entire model serialized inline and vanilla-JS/CSS UI (Flows board, Gallery, Data model, Glossary, Overview tabs, detail panel with source anchors). The primary human-facing read model, openable directly in a browser with no server or external deps.

sharedGlossary.label: Current selection (grounded)
sharedGlossary.description: The grounded projection of the selected node that a connected Claude session (or the SPA detail panel) reads: the node's label, type, description, the invariants it enforces, the flows it appears in, and the REAL source behind each anchor. Pull-based and always fresh -- computed on each request from the live in-memory selection, no polling or subscription.

sharedGlossary.label: Curated context bundle
sharedGlossary.description: The curated bundle projected to one grounded markdown document: each gathered node/flow/hotspot rendered with its description, invariants, flows, source anchors (real code), and for flows a colored Mermaid graph, joined by rules. This is what actor-claude reads. Exposed two ways: the MCP resource event-storming://selected-nodes (the domain-significant channel) and GET /api/context markdown for the SPA's 'Copy all' clipboard channel.

sharedGlossary.label: Local editor (VS Code)
sharedGlossary.description: The OS/editor outside the process boundary that handles vscode://file/... deep links. The sibling grounding path: instead of the inline excerpt, the viewer clicks the anchor's <a> href, and the OS hands the vscode:// URL to the editor, which opens the real file at the given line straight from the filesystem.

nodes.label: es-view Server Session
nodes.description: The single live node:http process the boot leaves running: it binds one loopback port and serves the React SPA, the JSON API, and the MCP endpoint over one shared in-memory state. Its lifecycle is this flow -- created at boot, resolves and holds the read-only model + indexes (services), initializes the mutable selection/bundle state, and listens until Ctrl+C. tactical.explanation: createServer() builds the http.createServer request router (MCP at /mcp, the /api/* endpoints, static SPA from distDir) closing over `resolved`, `state`, `services`, and `mcpHandler`. startServer() wraps it and calls tryListen(port, 20): server.listen(pnum, host); on EADDRINUSE with attemptsLeft>0 it retries pnum+1 (fall-forward from 5178, up to 20 attempts), else rejects; on success it sets runtime.baseUrl = `http://${host}:${pnum}` (so /api/mcp/* can print the exact connect command) and resolves { server, url, port }. buildServices(resolved) is the eager, never-rebuilt read model: { model, indexes: buildIndexes(model)={nodeById, hotspotById}, repoRoot }. nodes.label: ViewSource
nodes.description: Fetch the REAL code behind an anchor so the viewer can ground a command/aggregate/event/etc. sticky in the actual implementation. Given an anchor's { path, line }, return a small windowed excerpt (line +/- 8) read from the target repo, sandboxed to the repo root.

tactical.explanation: Read flow, no state change. Click path: the Anchor component's `view source` button toggles a lazy expander (Detail.jsx:100-104 toggle) that calls fetchSource(a.path, a.line) (src/web/api.js:35). fetchSource builds `GET /api/source?path&line&ctx` (api.js:37). The route handler (server.mjs:165) parses path/line/ctx, 400s if no path, else calls readSource(resolved.repoRoot, relPath, line, ctx) (src/server/source.mjs:13) and returns the result verbatim as JSON. readSource resolves abs = path.resolve(root, relPath), then reads the file and slices lines [ln-ctx .. ln+ctx] (ctx defaults to 8). SANDBOX GUARD (source.mjs:18): `if (abs !== root && !abs.startsWith(root + path.sep)) return { exists:false, error:'path escapes repo root' }` -- this prefix check is the ONLY thing stopping a caller from reading arbitrary files via ../ escapes; path.resolve normalizes ../ so plain traversal and absolute paths are caught. Note the guard uses path.resolve, not fs.realpath, so a symlink that lives inside repoRoot but points outside it would pass the check and be read (see notes). repoRoot is resolved once at boot by resolve-model.mjs (explicit --repo-root > model.meta.repoRoot > the model file's own tree > cwd) and frozen into `resolved`. There is NO authentication on this endpoint (or any /api route).

flows.name: Viewer opens the explorer and the SPA loads the whole model once
flows.summary: The viewer opens the es-view explorer in a browser. On mount the SPA fetches GET /api/model exactly once and the server returns the entire resolved model plus provenance meta from the snapshot it captured at startup -- minimal server work, one endpoint, no per-view queries. The SPA holds that single payload in one React context and re-derives every tab client-side (Flows board, Gallery, Data model, Glossary, Overview) via selectors shared with the server. The point is that the server is a thin model transport and the explorer's richness is all client-side derivation over ONE response.
flows.trigger: The viewer opens the es-view URL in a browser; the React App mounts and its boot useEffect fires.

flows.name: Operator rebuilds the bundled toy-shop example (npm run demo)
flows.summary: A thin orchestration wrapper. The operator runs `npm run demo`, which executes scripts/build-example.mjs. The script makes two synchronous execFileSync('node', ...) calls in order: first it invokes the merge CLI (merge-flows.js) over examples/toy-shop/traces to (re)write flows.json, then it invokes the view generator (generate-views.js) over that flows.json to (re)write flows.dot and explorer.html into examples/toy-shop/model. Because the calls are blocking and inherit exit status, a merge validation failure (exit 1) aborts before regeneration. The point is a one-command way to keep the shipped example -- which doubles as es-view's bundled fallback model -- in sync with its trace set.

flows.name: A connected Claude session reads the live model/selection/bundle over MCP
flows.summary: A Claude session that has registered the es-view MCP server reads the live domain model to ground a refactor. Over the streamable-HTTP /mcp transport it calls tools (get_current_selection, get_node, get_flow, list_model, list_data_model) and reads the event-storming://selected-nodes resource. Each projection is served from the SAME in-memory state the human drives in the SPA: the selection/bundle (agg-selection) and the merged model (agg-model). The grounded projections pull REAL source excerpts from the filesystem behind each anchor, so Claude sees actual code, not just labels. Nothing is written: this is a pure read that lets Claude act on 'the selected node' or 'the gathered context'.
flows.trigger: A connected Claude session (registered via `claude mcp add` and initialized over /mcp) calls an MCP tool (get_current_selection / get_node / get_flow / list_model / list_data_model) or reads the `event-storming://selected-nodes` resource.

flows.name: Viewer curates a context bundle for a connected Claude session
flows.summary: In the explorer SPA the human gathers a set of nodes, whole flows, and hotspots into a 'context bundle' by clicking 'Add to context' or right-clicking items. Each add is validated (the item must exist for its type) and stored in an insertion-ordered set in the server's in-memory state, the same object the MCP bridge reads. The bundle is projected on demand to one grounded markdown document (descriptions, invariants, flows, real source, Mermaid graphs) and handed to Claude two ways: as the @-mentionable MCP resource event-storming://selected-nodes, and as the SPA's 'Copy all' clipboard export. The point is to let the human assemble exactly the slice of the model a refactor conversation needs, grounded in actual files.
flows.trigger: The viewer clicks '+ Add to context' on a node/flow, or right-clicks a node/flow/hotspot and picks 'Add to context bundle', in the explorer SPA.

flows.name: Operator boots the es-view explorer server
flows.summary: The operator runs `npx event-storming-recovery` / `es-view` (or `npm run preview`). es-view parses its args, resolves a servable model (explicit --model, an on-the-fly --traces merge, an auto-discovered flows.json, or the bundled toy-shop example), builds an eager read-only index over it, and initializes an empty in-memory selection/bundle state. It then stands up ONE local node:http server -- SPA + JSON API + MCP endpoint over that shared state -- binding the first free port at/after 5178, prints the connect banner (including the exact `claude mcp add` line), and opens the browser. The result is a live session a human can explore and a Claude terminal can attach to.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `npx event-storming-recovery [view] [options]`, `es-view`, or `npm run preview` (which builds then runs `node bin/es-view.mjs`).

flows.name: Human selects a node in the explorer; Claude reads it live
flows.summary: This is the selection bridge, the heart of the tool. The human opens any node's detail in the SPA (from the flows board, overview, gallery, glossary, data-model tab, a detail-panel nav row, or a bundle row), and the store's openDetail mirrors that node to the server via POST /api/selection. The server validates the id against the merged model and stores it in a purely in-memory Selection aggregate shared same-process with the MCP server. A connected Claude session then pulls the current selection through the get_current_selection MCP tool, which grounds it (invariants, flows, and the real source behind each anchor) via context.mjs. Push-on-click by the human, pull-on-call by Claude -- no poll, no subscription.
flows.trigger: The human opens a node's detail anywhere in the SPA (openDetail), which posts it to /api/selection. It fires from the Flows board (Board.jsx), Overview (Overview.jsx), Gallery (Gallery.jsx), Glossary (Glossary.jsx), Data-model tab (DataModel.jsx), Detail-panel nav rows (Detail.jsx), and context-bundle rows (ContextBundle.jsx).

flows.name: Operator generates the DOT + explorer views from the model
flows.summary: The operator runs es-generate over a merged flows.json and an output directory. The tool reads the model once and projects it into two human-facing read models without mutating any domain state: a Graphviz DOT board (one cluster per flow, physical storage nodes excluded) and a self-contained explorer.html that inlines the whole model and a dependency-free SPA. Both artifacts are written to the output directory and embed vscode:// deep links back into the analyzed checkout. The point is to turn the abstract model into something a human can open in a browser or Graphviz and click straight to source.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `node tools/generate-views.js <flows.json> <outDir> --repo-root <abs> --title "..."` (via the `es-generate` bin, or `npm run demo` -> scripts/build-example.mjs).

flows.name: Viewer copies grounded markdown to the clipboard for Claude
flows.summary: From several places in the explorer (a node detail panel, a flow header, a right-click menu, or the context-bundle drawer) the viewer hits a 'Copy for Claude' button. The SPA calls GET /api/item (or GET /api/context for the whole bundle), the server reads the in-memory model and slices the real source behind each anchor from disk, and returns grounded markdown, a flow item also embedding a Mermaid graph. The handler writes that markdown to the OS clipboard so the viewer can paste it straight into a Claude session. This is the manual clipboard channel, the parallel 'give it to Claude' path to the server-persisted MCP context bundle.
flows.trigger: Viewer clicks a 'Copy for Claude' / 'Copy all for Claude' button (detail panel, flow header, right-click context menu, or bundle drawer).

flows.name: Operator merges per-flow traces into the validated model
flows.summary: The operator runs es-merge (or es-view --traces) over a directory of per-flow trace JSONs. The tool reads every trace, unions the shared nodes by global id and accumulates the flows, hotspots, and terms into one canonical model, then validates the whole graph against its invariants. On success it writes (or holds in memory) the validated flows.json that the server and generator consume; on any error it refuses (server) or writes-then-flags (CLI). The point is to let independent trace agents converge on one consistent, referentially closed model.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `node tools/merge-flows.js <tracesDir> <outFile>` (or `es-merge`), or es-view resolves a model from `--traces <dir>`.

flows.name: Viewer connects their Claude terminal from the explorer
flows.summary: In the explorer's ConnectClaude panel the viewer picks a scope and clicks 'Add to Claude'. The SPA POSTs /api/mcp/register; the server resolves its own live MCP URL, whitelists the scope, and shells out `claude mcp add --transport http event-storming "<url>/mcp" [--scope <scope>]` on the host as the same OS user. On success the app is registered as an MCP server in the user's Claude config and the viewer is told to run /mcp. The point is one-click wiring of the running app into the user's Claude terminal, but the mechanism (a browser click spawning a host process that runs the user's CLI) is the single most surprising write in the app.
flows.trigger: Viewer clicks 'Add to Claude' in the ConnectClaude panel (scope dropdown: local/project/user).

flows.name: Viewer grounds a sticky in the real code behind its anchor
flows.summary: Every command/aggregate/event/etc. sticky in the explorer carries source anchors. When the viewer clicks an anchor's 'view source', the SPA calls GET /api/source?path&line&ctx; the server's readSource resolves the path against the frozen repo root, rejects anything escaping it, and returns a windowed excerpt (line +/- 8) read straight from the target repo's files. The excerpt renders inline beneath the anchor. A sibling grounding path skips the server entirely: the same anchor is an <a href='vscode://file/...'> deep link, so the OS/editor can open the real file at that line. Both paths turn an abstract sticky into the actual code, one inline (via the filesystem through the sandboxed API) and one by jumping to the editor.
flows.trigger: Viewer clicks 'view source' on an anchor in a node/hotspot detail (or clicks the anchor's vscode:// link to jump to their editor).

hotspots.label: The explorer loads the model once at boot; edits need a page reload AND a server restart
hotspots.description: The SPA fetches /api/model exactly once (App boot useEffect, empty deps) and never re-fetches -- no polling, websocket, or live-reload. The server serves the model snapshot resolved at startup and builds its indexes eagerly, so it never picks up file changes either. Result: after editing flows.json (or the traces feeding --traces), the viewer sees nothing new until the operator BOTH restarts es-view (to re-resolve + re-index) AND reloads the page (to re-fetch). Human question: is a one-shot frozen boot acceptable for the curate-while-you-work loop this tool is built for, or should es-view watch the model file and the SPA poll / offer a reload affordance?

tactical.explanation: App.jsx useEffect has [] deps and an alive guard -- exactly one fetch per page load, no interval or socket. server.mjs GET /api/model returns resolved.model captured in the createServer closure; buildServices runs buildIndexes once at startup (bin/es-view.mjs main); resolveModel likewise runs once. Nothing invalidates or rebuilds either the payload or the indexes for the process lifetime.

hotspots.label: npm run demo overwrites the shipped fallback model in place with no backup or gate
hotspots.description: The demo regenerates examples/toy-shop/model/{flows.json,flows.dot,explorer.html} directly over the shipped files. That same examples/toy-shop/model/flows.json is es-view's 4th-tier bundled fallback (resolve-model.mjs:92), served whenever a user runs es-view with no model of their own. So the quality of the shipped default is only as good as the toy-shop trace set at demo time, and there is no backup, diff, or review gate before the shipped artifact is replaced. Compounding it: es-merge (hot-invalid-model-written) writes flows.json BEFORE checking validation errors, so a toy-shop trace edit that fails validation would still leave a written flows.json on disk (the chain then aborts before generate-views, so flows.dot/explorer.html would be stale relative to it) -- and if that broken flows.json is committed, es-view ships a broken default. Human question: should the demo (or the package's prepack/CI) validate and guard the regenerated toy-shop model -- e.g. fail the build on merge errors, or verify the artifacts against a golden snapshot -- before it can become the shipped fallback?

tactical.explanation: scripts/build-example.mjs writes straight into examples/toy-shop/model (the packaged example dir, listed in package.json files[]). resolve-model.mjs tier 4 resolves sourcePath = packageRoot/examples/toy-shop/model/flows.json as the bundled example; bin/es-view.mjs advertises the fallback to the bundled toy-shop example when no model is found here. No test in the demo path asserts the regenerated artifacts before they overwrite the shipped ones (smoke.test.mjs merges the traces but does not gate the demo).

hotspots.label: The context bundle is one process-global set, not per-session
hotspots.description: The bundle (like the selection) lives in a single in-memory Map on the shared state object -- one bundle per es-view process, keyed by nothing but type:id. Every browser tab and every connected MCP/Claude session reads and mutates the SAME bundle. With the default 127.0.0.1 bind this is just 'one human, one run', but es-view can bind --host 0.0.0.0, at which point multiple viewers would stomp each other's bundle and a connected Claude would see a racy union of everyone's curation via the selected-nodes resource. Human question: is the bundle intended to be a single shared workspace for one run, or should it be scoped per browser session / per MCP connection before the server is ever exposed beyond localhost?

tactical.explanation: state.mjs createState() holds one `bundle` Map with no session/tab/connection key; server.mjs and mcp.mjs both close over the same state instance (bin/es-view.mjs passes one state to startServer and createMcpHandler). The MCP resource handler renders renderBundleMarkdown(services, state.getBundle()) over that shared bundle. There is no per-session partitioning anywhere on the add/read path.

hotspots.label: Port fall-forward makes the pinned MCP URL stale
hotspots.description: startServer falls forward from 5178 to 5179+ on EADDRINUSE (up to 20 attempts) and prints whatever port it landed on -- but the plugin-declared MCP server (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and .mcp.json.example hardcode http://127.0.0.1:5178/mcp, and the explorer skill (skills/event-storming-explorer/SKILL.md) states the app 'must run on port 5178' and tells the user to free 5178 if it is taken. So if 5178 is occupied, es-view silently serves on 5179 while the pinned MCP config points at the wrong server (or nothing), and the banner's `claude mcp add ... {url}/mcp` line contradicts the pinned config. Human question: should the fall-forward be removed (fail hard when 5178 is taken, matching the pinned URL), or should the plugin/MCP registration be made port-dynamic? The two designs disagree today.

tactical.explanation: server.mjs startServer/tryListen(port,20): on EADDRINUSE with attemptsLeft>0 it retries pnum+1, else rejects; runtime.baseUrl and the printed banner use the actual bound port. plugin.json and .mcp.json.example both pin :5178; SKILL.md hard-codes the 5178 assumption. The runtime is dynamic, the declared MCP endpoint is static.

There is no file watcher and no invalidation, so editing flows.json or re-running es-merge has no effect until the operator restarts es-view -- even though the explorer is meant for live, iterative work with Claude. Human question: is a static boot snapshot intended (restart to refresh), or should es-view watch the model file / --traces dir and rebuild the model+indexes on change?

hotspots.label: --host is an unauthenticated passthrough (0.0.0.0 exposes the API + MCP)
hotspots.description: --host is passed straight to server.listen with no authentication anywhere on the API or MCP surface. The 127.0.0.1 default is safe, but `--host 0.0.0.0` (or a LAN IP) exposes to the network the full unauthenticated JSON API -- including GET /api/source, which streams any file under repoRoot -- and the MCP endpoint that a Claude session drives, plus POST /api/mcp/register which shells out `claude mcp add`. Human question: should es-view refuse a non-loopback host (or require auth / warn loudly) before binding to 0.0.0.0? Note /api/source IS sandboxed to repoRoot with a traversal guard, so the exposure is the whole repo tree, not the arbitrary filesystem.

tactical.explanation: parseArgs takes --host (default 127.0.0.1) and passes it verbatim to startServer -> server.listen(pnum, host). No route checks Origin, a token, or the bound host. readSource guards against ../ escapes (abs must stay under path.resolve(repoRoot)), bounding /api/source to the repo tree. mcp-register.mjs's claudeMcpAdd is invoked by POST /api/mcp/register with no auth.

hotspots.label: Closing the detail panel never clears the selection server-side, so Claude sees a stale node
hotspots.description: When the human closes the detail panel, the SPA's closeDetail clears only React state (setSelectedNodeId(null); setDetail(null)); it does NOT tell the server. The server (and therefore the MCP get_current_selection tool) keeps the LAST selected node indefinitely, so a connected Claude session will report the human is "looking at" a node they already dismissed. A clean path exists but is unused: DELETE /api/selection -> state.clearSelection() is wired on the server, and the SPA client even has no wrapper for it (pushSelection only ever POSTs an id). Human question: should closeDetail clear the server selection (POST/DELETE null on close), or is holding the last-viewed node the intended behavior for Claude's continuity? If holding is intended, get_current_selection arguably should signal that the panel is closed (staleness/age) rather than present the node as currently-open.

tactical.explanation: store.jsx closeDetail (line 46) = `setSelectedNodeId(null); setDetail(null)` only -- no api call. There is no DELETE /api/selection caller anywhere in src/web (grep: the only /api/selection reference in api.js is pushSelection's POST). Server-side, state.clearSelection() (state.mjs:18) is wired to DELETE /api/selection (server.mjs:135) but nothing invokes it. Meanwhile get_current_selection (mcp.mjs:30) reads state.getSelection() live, so it returns the last node set until the process ends or a new node is opened. The selection's `at` timestamp is captured (state.mjs:17) but never surfaced to Claude, so there is not even an age hint to detect the staleness.

hotspots.label: Unauthenticated GET /api/source is an arbitrary-file-read primitive if bound to 0.0.0.0
hotspots.description: es-view binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, but --host accepts any address including 0.0.0.0. There is no authentication on any /api route, and GET /api/source reads an arbitrary repo-relative file and returns its contents. The ONLY thing scoping it is the path-escape prefix guard in readSource (abs must equal repoRoot or start with repoRoot + sep). Bound to 0.0.0.0, anyone on the network can read every file under repoRoot (source, .env, secrets committed in the tree, etc.). Two gaps widen it: (1) the guard uses path.resolve, not fs.realpath, so a symlink inside repoRoot pointing outside it would pass the check and leak files beyond the root; (2) repoRoot often IS the user's whole working tree (default cwd). Human question: should es-view refuse --host 0.0.0.0 (or any non-loopback bind) without an explicit opt-in / auth token, and should readSource realpath-check to defeat symlink escapes? Or is this strictly a localhost dev tool where a non-loopback bind is user-accepted risk?

(server.mjs:202). GET /api/source (server.mjs:165) calls readSource(resolved.repoRoot, relPath, line, ctx). The sandbox is the single guard at source.mjs:18: `if (abs !== root && !abs.startsWith(root + path.sep)) return { exists:false, error:'path escapes repo root' }`. path.resolve normalizes ../ and absolute paths (both caught), but does not resolve symlinks, so an in-root symlink to an out-of-root target is read. repoRoot defaults to cwd (resolve-model.mjs:99-102).

terms.definition: A person or role that issues commands and reads read models to decide (Viewer, Operator, a connected Claude session). Actor is the softest color convention on a wall (a small yellow), and in a flat digital diagram it needs a genuinely different hue from the aggregate to stay distinct.

A consistency boundary: state that changes together and enforces its own invariants. In Event Storming an aggregate only RECEIVES commands and EMITS events, never issues a command. In a services-and-repositories codebase there are no explicit aggregates, so the data-layer scout recovers them as clusters of entities that change together (they are almost always 'inferred').

The zoom level at which the same action is modeled. A generic 'cmd-attach-file' in a file-attachment pattern flow and a specialized 'cmd-attach-files-to-line' inline in an ordering flow are the same action at two altitudes. The merge deliberately does NOT force-merge legitimate altitude variations: collapsing them breaks the ability to walk each flow as a self-contained story. Shared aggregates and external systems, not collapsed commands, carry the connective tissue between flows.

A pointer from a model node to a specific place in the source: { path, line, symbol, note }. `symbol` (method/handler/class) is the durable part since line numbers rot across rebases. Anchors are what grounding reads through to fetch real code, what the SPA turns into vscode:// deep links, and what MCP tool results inline. A cross-cutting term the whole tool uses, not owned by one node.

A strategic boundary within which the ubiquitous language is consistent; edges that cross it are the integration points (an anti-corruption layer or published language). A bounded context must be DECLARED with an explicit label, never inferred from namespace/folder layout, because code layout is an accident rather than a domain fact. A code-derived view cannot recover context grouping on its own, which is one of the things it structurally loses versus a workshop wall.

How the physical tier nests: a column points to its table, a table to its database, a database to its server, via a 'parent' pointer rather than a flow edge. This repo packaged as a Claude Code plugin, declared by `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Installing it bundles both skills, the prompts/tools, and the `event-storming` MCP server declaration (pinned to http://127.0.0.1:5178/mcp) in one step, so an installed user gets the whole workflow plus the context bridge without wiring anything by hand.

terms.definition: Strictly reactive logic: "whenever <event> then <command>." It sits after an event and before the next command, orchestrating cross-aggregate reactions. This repo adds a 'synchronous' flag: a synchronous policy is inline synchronous code reacting to the first event (not a decoupled subscriber), which is how the UI-vs-service split rule models a second write with its own failure window.

The server's port-selection behavior: it tries the preferred port (default 5178) and, on EADDRINUSE, increments and retries up to 20 times, then binds and prints whatever port it landed on. Convenient for running several explorers at once, but it means the live MCP URL can differ from any hardcoded one (see hotspot hot-port-fall-forward-stale-mcp).

An append-only list on a field (and on physical nodes) recording HOW each piece of evidence was obtained: sql-literal, connection-string, orm-mapping, migration, inferred-from-dto, or assumed. Provenance appends, never overwrites, so a migration that corroborates a sql-literal finding raises confidence while the original code evidence stays. In this tool's own self-model, storage is recovered from file/in-memory reads rather than SQL, so its fields lean toward inferred-from-dto / assumed rather than sql-literal.

The first move of a deep-trace: confirm the entry point is actually wired (a caller exists, the route is registered, the button renders, DI is set up) before tracing it. When a caller is missing, chasing git log / git show recovers when and why it was removed, which is often the most valuable finding; the result sets the flow's status (live / dead / superseded). This is how dead and superseded flows get caught rather than modeled as if current.

terms.definition: What an actor reads in order to decide: a grid, view, projection, or downloaded file. It is the query side, distinct from the command/write side, and carries a demand-driven fields[] list describing what data it returns and where that data comes from.

Depth and fan-out are aggressive; convergence (a child that returns without changing the model) is the brake. The return contract is fixed - artifacts to files, conclusions + anchors back - so a deep subtree still lands in the parent's context as a short summary. terms.definition: The single domain node the human is currently looking at in the explorer, held in memory as `{ nodeId, at }`. It is pull-based and always fresh: the grounded projection (label, type, description, enforced invariants, flows, real source behind each anchor) is recomputed on each read of `get_current_selection` or GET /api/selection. Exactly one node at a time; setting a new one replaces the last.

The tool's core trick: the human clicks a node in the browser, the SPA mirrors that choice to the server's shared in-memory state, and a connected Claude session reads it through the MCP `get_current_selection` tool. Because the web UI and the MCP server run in the SAME process and close over the same `state`, no polling or subscription is needed. This is what lets a Claude terminal know 'the selected node' the user is pointing at.

The set of agreed global node ids for a target system's recurring concepts (its core aggregates, external systems, and actor roles), handed to every trace agent before tracing so independent agents converge on the same ids (agg-order, not order / customer-order / orders-aggregate) instead of inventing synonyms. It is the input convention that makes the finished flows join into one map. terms.definition: One entry in a field's sources[] array wiring the field to a physical column (or a raw dotted address) it draws from, tagged with a role and a transform. A source ref that looks like a local node id (col- tbl- db- srv-) MUST resolve to a known node or the merge errors; a free-form address string is accepted as-is.

The enum on a field source saying HOW that column relates to the field: 'derived-from' when it populates the field, 'filtered-by' / 'joined-on' / 'grouped-by' when it only influences the field, 'constant' for a fixed value. Nonstandard values merge as warnings, not errors.

The React single-page app es-view serves as static files from dist/web (with SPA fallback to index.html). It fetches the model once from /api/model, holds it in one React context, and re-derives every tab (Board, Data-model, Glossary, Gallery, Detail) from it. It is the browser half of the selection bridge: clicks here POST to /api/selection and /api/context. Distinct from the standalone explorer.html the generator emits.

One card on the Event Storming wall: a single command, aggregate, event, policy, read model, actor, external system, or invariant. In this tool a sticky is realized as a node in flows.json (behavioral stickies are colored by the event-storming palette). Value Objects and Entities are NOT stickies; tactical structure is implied on the wall, not drawn.

The two registers the model moves between. STRATEGIC = what the system does, why, and how its flows connect (the recovered Event Storming view). TACTICAL = how it is actually implemented: the call chain, key methods, data touched, carried on every behavioral node as a 'tactical' block of explanation + source anchors. Every sticky keeps tactical anchors precisely so a reader can move between the two planes freely; a strategic node with no way back to code is a dead end.

The MCP transport es-view mounts at POST /mcp, via the SDK's StreamableHTTPServerTransport with enableJsonResponse. An `initialize` POST spins up a session and issues an Mcp-Session-Id; later POST/GET/DELETE reuse the transport for that session. Every session's tools close over the same shared services + state, so the live selection is always what Claude reads.

The canonical strategic Event Storming model: the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta, assembled by the merge and serialized as flows.json. It is the single source of truth every view is generated from and the es-view server / MCP bridge read; views are disposable, flows.json is edited (via traces) and regenerated. Modeled in this self-model as the aggregate agg-model.

terms.definition: A flow's coverage depth. Tier-1 is an individually traced domain flow (traced end to end on its own). The triage phase decides which candidate flows are Tier-1 vs collapsed into a Tier-2 exemplar.

terms.definition: A single per-flow trace document ({ nodes, flows, hotspots, terms }) that a deep-trace agent writes to the traces directory for one flow. terms.definition: The enum on a field source naming the OPERATION applied to the column on its way into the field: identity, transformation, aggregation, join, filter, lookup, or constant. It is orthogonal to role (role = why the column matters; transform = what is done to it). Nonstandard values merge as warnings.

This repo's key modeling stance: the command/aggregate/event/policy grammar fits TRANSACTIONAL domains (intent that can be rejected), but a dataflow/ETL/pipeline stretch is a different plane that continuously transforms immutable records and cannot reject anything. Model the two planes joined at a named seam (an anti-corruption/translation step): everything on the dataflow side is plumbing kept in a command's tactical detail, and only domain-significant facts crossing the seam are promoted to events. In this self-model the merge and generate steps are ETL kept single-plane for exactly this reason.

anchors.symbol: Conventions: dataflow stages are not aggregates

terms.definition: The shared domain vocabulary that the code, the model, and the people all use for the same concept. The per-flow tactical accumulation on a shared node.
